article.title: Dar stresses need for uninterrupted energy supplies amid regional tensions
article.summary: Deputy Prime Minister and Foreign Minister Ishaq Dar held a telephone conversation with Iranian Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi on Saturday, with the two discussing the latest developments in the region, according to the Foreign Office.During the conversation, Dar stressed the importance of ensuring uninterrupted energy supplies and the safe and expeditious passage of ships, citing their significance for developing countries and global supply chains.He also underscored the need for dialogue and diplomacy, saying they remain the only viable means of ensuring peace and stability in the region.Dar and Araghchi agreed to maintain close cooperation and to meet in New York on the sidelines of the 81st session of the United Nations General Assembly.Before the Iran war started on February 28, the Strait of Hormuz typically handled about 125 large, commercial vessels per day, including tankers, gas carriers, bulkers and container vessels, accounting for some 20% of the world’s daily crude oi...

article.title: Pakistan and Iran foreign ministers discuss regional stability and safe shipping
article.summary: Pakistan and Iran foreign ministers discuss regional stability and safe shippingPakistan’s Foreign Minister Ishaq Dar and his Iranian counterpart, Abbas Araghchi, spoke by phone to discuss recent regional developments, Islamabad confirmed in a statement.During the call, Dar emphasised the critical need for secure shipping routes and uninterrupted energy supplies, warning of the potential fallout for developing nations and global supply chains. He further stressed that "dialogue and diplomacy" remain the only viable paths to regional peace.The two diplomats agreed to maintain close cooperation and are scheduled to meet in person in New York on the sidelines of the 81st UN General Assembly.

article.title: Pakistan calls for halt to Houthi attacks on merchant vessels
article.summary: Pakistan has condemned attacks by Yemen’s Houthi militia on merchant vessels and seafarers in the Bab al-Mandab Strait, calling for their immediate cessation and stressing the need to safeguard freedom of navigation and commercial shipping.

article.title: Houthis urged to halt ‘provocative acts’ in Red Sea
article.summary: WASHINGTON: Pakistan condemned Houthi attacks on merchant shipping in the Bab al Mandab Strait and called for their immediate cessation, as the UN Security Council held its second discussion on Friday on the escalating threat to the strategic waterway in the wake of renewed hostilities.“We call upon Houthi militia for immediate cessation of these provocative acts which could have dire consequences for maritime security, and regional peace and stability,” Pakistan’s Permanent Representative to the UN, Ambassador Asim Iftikhar Ahmad, told a Security Council meeting convened by Bahrain.The meeting came two days after the Security Council was briefed on the rapidly deteriorating situation around Bab al Mandab, where the Houthis have advanced along Yemen’s western coast and reportedly captured several islands in the southern Red Sea.United Nations Assistant Secretary General Khaled Khiari told the council that the situation in and around the strait had become “increasingly volatile”.Paki...
